clue.text: Sauce displayed by jazz enthusiasts appearing for trial

parts.note: cats is old slang for jazz fans and players
a defendant who is up before the court is appearing for trial

explanation.surface: A group of jazz fans produce a bottle of sauce in the dock at their court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' simply joins the definition to the two pieces. The answer is the mainly American spelling of the tomato sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of ketchup, the tomato condiment.

clue.text: It's something like a lounge, a fanciful design

indicators.note: a fanciful design is an imaginative new arrangement, here of the letters just before it

explanation.surface: An estate agent hedges about a whimsically decorated room that is almost a lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fanciful design' asks for A LOUNGE A to be rearranged. The definition is the opening phrase, not a description of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that resembles or corresponds to another is its counterpart or parallel.

clue.text: Extraordinary individual!

definitions.meaning: remarkable or exceptional, as in a person of rare courage
single, relating to just one, as in the grammatical number that is not plural

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym both for remarkable and for relating to a single one.

clue.text: Two women said it's used to form synthetic fibres

definitions.text: it's used to form synthetic fibres

indicators.note: said tells us the two names are spoken, and what is heard is entered

parts.note: Polly and Esther are two women's names

explanation.surface: A pair of women explain what goes into man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes two women's names, spoken one after the other, give the sound of the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a polymer spun into man-made textile thread.

clue.text: Tradesman that's initially unwilling to be limited by creditor

indicators.note: what is limited by something has that thing as its boundaries on both sides

parts.note: Cr is the bookkeeping abbreviation for creditor

indicators.note: initially here places the reluctant word first, ahead of the letters for that's

parts.note: loth means reluctant
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper at first resists having his spending capped by someone he owes money to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' is not a first-letter signal here: it says which of the two inner pieces comes first. 'to be limited by' sets the creditor's abbreviation as the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a maker or seller of cloth and garments is one kind of trader.

clue.text: Precise reference to canons in dean's novel upset priest

parts.note: the canons of a cathedral collectively form its chapter

indicators.note: in places the turned priest inside the rearranged letters of the dean
novel means new, so the letters of the neighbouring word take a new order

parts.note: the letters DEANS, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down clue the priest is written upwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a title for a priest

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean's book, with its exact citations of church law, has annoyed a fellow clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clerical surface hides that 'canons' are a cathedral's clergy, not church laws, and that 'novel' means new. In a down clue 'upset' writes the priest's title upwards, and 'in' sets it within ANDSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to give this is to cite the exact source and authority for a statement.

clue.text: Man crossing ancient city is in the travel industry

indicators.note: crossing means the man's name spans the other pieces, going round them

parts.note: Tom is a man's name
Ur, the Sumerian city, is the standard crossword ancient city

explanation.surface: A man who makes his way across an old city works in the holiday trade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the business of holidays and sightseeing.

clue.text: One moans in the throes of sleeplessness

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: throes are violent convulsions, so the words before are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies groaning through a wretched wakeful night.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' looks like part of the phrase 'in the throes of' but is fodder, leaving 'the throes of' to signal the rearrangement that makes NSOMNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the medical name for the inability to sleep.

clue.text: Booming old thing talking about a collection of books

parts.note: res is Latin for thing, as in res publica, hence an old word for it
a lecturer on a subject is talking about it
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A loud-voiced old character holds forth about his library.
explanation.walkthrough: A straight run of four pieces; 'old' marks the thing as Latin rather than supplying an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a deep, echoing voice or sound is described this way.

clue.text: Replaced first-class pine with a minute tree

indicators.note: replaced is read as put back, so the whole run of pieces is written backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means top quality
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: A gardener swaps a fine conifer for a tiny sapling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' turns the whole run AI LONG A M back to front. 'pine' is the verb to yearn, not the conifer, and 'minute' is the unit of time, not tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a tree or shrub with large waxy flowers.

clue.text: Sharks in harbours?

definitions.meaning: a kind of slow bottom-dwelling shark has this name
as a verb: one who harbours a grudge keeps it alive and tends it

explanation.definitionFit: Example of a shark species, and a synonym for cherishes or fosters a feeling.

clue.text: Written record in a London column

definitions.meaning: an older sense: a document or lasting written memorial
the tall stone pillar in the City of London marking the Great Fire of 1666 is known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense of a document, and the name of the Great Fire memorial pillar.

clue.text: Collier, the old PM's sound valet

indicators.note: sound tells us the prime minister's name is heard, not spelt as he wrote it

parts.note: William Pitt, the Elder or the Younger, was a British prime minister in the eighteenth century
a gentleman's valet is his man

explanation.surface: A coal miner turns out to be the trusty manservant of a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns the prime minister's name PITT into PIT. The surface reads 'sound' as reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words name a coal miner.

clue.text: A new cafe lacking a place for waiters

parts.note: the A as written, then n, the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: lacking says the word for a cafe goes without the letter named next

parts.note: a tearoom is a small cafe

explanation.surface: A newly opened cafe has nowhere for its serving staff to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' drops one letter from the seven-letter word for a cafe. The waiters are people who wait, not restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: it is the outer chamber where visitors sit until they are called in.

clue.text: I become angry about member upholding gold standard

indicators.note: in a down clue, what upholds the gold sits beneath it and holds it up

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: about puts the words for my getting angry around the member

parts.note: to flame is to blaze up in anger
M abbreviates member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A speaker loses their temper over an MP who defends the gold standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholding' puts OR on top in this down entry, and 'about' wraps I FLAME round M. The 'gold standard' is split: only 'standard', a banner, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it was the red banner of the old French kings.

clue.text: Sly look of Republican general at the front

indicators.note: at the front tells us the general comes first, ahead of the Republican

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A senior officer of the governing party gives a crafty glance from the battle line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' orders the pieces: LEE first, then R. 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sidelong, suggestive glance.

clue.text: Sort of traffic man giving money, say, to father

indicators.note: say tells us the slang for money is spoken rather than spelt that way

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Some kind of traffic official hands cash to his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives LOLLI from the sound of LOLLY. In Britain a lollipop man is a school crossing patrol, named for his round stop sign on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Compound: the word goes before man to name a British school crossing patrol.

clue.text: Noble eastern city largely accepting a form of taxation

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened city takes the tax inside itself
largely means most of the city's name is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, England
VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A stately city in the east mostly puts up with a new kind of levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like it describes the city but is the definition. 'largely' trims the city's last letter before 'accepting' lets the tax in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lofty or exalted in character or rank.

clue.text: Scottish engineer taking water from French painter

indicators.note: taking means the water is removed from the painter's name

parts.note: Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French painter
eau is the French word for water, familiar from eau de toilette

explanation.surface: A Scots engineer helps himself to a French artist's water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' removes EAU from WATTEAU; 'French' quietly hints that the water is in French too.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: James, the Scot who improved the steam engine.

clue.text: Literary work with bands round it

indicators.note: round means the bands encircle the short word that follows

parts.note: rings are bands, such as wedding bands

explanation.surface: A bound volume of literature has straps fastened around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective sense: an author's output taken together.

clue.text: Material for caustic article about the French

indicators.note: about means the sharp word and the article go around the French word

parts.note: a tart remark is a sharp, caustic one
la is the French word for the
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone gathers notes for a biting newspaper piece on France's people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a kind of cloth, not research for a piece of journalism; 'about' is the container signal and 'for' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a thin, stiff open-weave muslin.

clue.text: Border fort in chaos before the first signs of enemy raids

indicators.note: before says the disordered letters come ahead of the two initials
chaos is disorder, so the two words before it are thrown into a new order
the first signs of two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A stronghold on the boundary is in disarray as the first attacks begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder alongside the fort, not a link: 'chaos' makes FRONTI of them, set 'before' the initials that 'the first signs of' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the boundary between two countries.

clue.text: Roll up on horse, it being some distance

parts.note: to furl a sail or flag is to roll it up
G, said gee, is a child's word for a horse, as in gee-gee

explanation.surface: A racegoer arrives on horseback after a fair old ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is apt: the distance is the unit in which British horse races are measured, an eighth of a mile. 'it being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a unit of length, 220 yards.

clue.text: King wearing Roman historian's distinctive clothing

indicators.note: the king wearing the historian has the historian's name around him like a garment

parts.note: Livy wrote the great history of Rome
ER is Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch dresses up in the striking robes of an ancient chronicler.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'wearing', the wearer is on the inside: the king sits within the historian's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the uniform that marks out a household's servants or a company's vehicles.

clue.text: Capricious little creature nursing injured tail

indicators.note: nursing means the small animal holds the other letters within itself

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters of the next word are put out of order

explanation.surface: A temperamental small animal licks its wounded tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges TAIL into ATIL, which VOLE holds, as 'nursing' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liable to change mood suddenly.

clue.text: No right to share the medicine

indicators.note: no right means the word for a share appears with its R missing

parts.note: a portion is a share

explanation.surface: A patient is told they are not entitled to a dose of the remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes R out of PORTION; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a liquid dose of something healing or magical.

clue.text: Curious, during tea break, to indulge in deep thought

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
in can mean during, as in in the night

indicators.note: break means the word before it is broken up and reset in another order

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person spends the afternoon pause pondering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' is odd, not inquisitive, and 'during' is a piece, not a container signal. 'break' reorders the drink into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ponder or chew something over at length.

clue.text: Descent from pier edge when blown off

indicators.note: what is blown off is scattered, so the letters of the two words before land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles from the end of a jetty in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown off' rearranges PIER EDGE. 'Descent' is ancestry, not a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a line of ancestry or lineage.

clue.text: Directions given by an ascetic in the old days

definitions.text: an ascetic in the old days

parts.note: compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial
compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial
compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial
compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial
compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial
compass points: east, south, south, east, north, east, each as its initial

explanation.surface: An ancient hermit tells travellers which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is a string of six compass points. 'given by' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of an austere Jewish sect of the time of Christ.
